findings.body:
Removed `os.path.basename` sanitization and now passes an attacker-controlled `request.args.get("path", name)` value straight into `os.path.join(REPORTS, ...)`. An attacker can request `/reports/x?path=../../../etc/passwd` and `send_file` will serve files outside `/srv/reports`.

```suggestion
    safe = os.path.normpath(request.args.get("path", name)).lstrip(os.sep)
    if safe.startswith("..") or os.path.isabs(safe):
        abort(400)
    return send_file(os.path.join(REPORTS, safe))
```

summary: The change removes the only path sanitization and introduces an unsanitized `path` query parameter directly into `send_file`. This opens a path-traversal vulnerability on the `/reports/<name>` route.

verification.reason: The change removed `os.path.basename(name)` and now joins attacker-controlled `request.args.get("path", name)` directly into `os.path.join(REPORTS, ...)`, so `?path=../../../etc/passwd` can escape `/srv/reports` via `send_file`. This is a real critical path-traversal regression.
